title: App Activity Table Columns
lede: The report now answers iOS support questions directly while keeping repeated browser installations from stretching a single user row across the screen.

stats.n: iOS hardware, iOS software, latest browser, and last seen are explicit
12 installations summarized as latest browser plus a count
Same authenticated preview session and roster dataset

sections.heading: Matched authenticated capture
sections.note: Same preview database, signed-in owner, browser origin, viewport, and roster data. The before capture renders the source-control page; the after capture renders the updated page.

pairs.title: Table top
pairs.sub: Look at the headers and Erik Role's row: the repeated web clients disappear, while both iOS clients remain legible.
pairs.beforeCap: The old Clients and device column repeats every web installation, and iOS build information is separated into a second ambiguous column.
pairs.afterCap: Dedicated iOS hardware, iOS software, Latest browser, and Last seen columns keep the support signals readable in one row.

changesNote: This is a presentation-only slice. The API payload, owner allowlist, privacy boundary, and build-comparison semantics stay unchanged.

changes.h: Web activity was repeated per installation
changes.was: A user with many web installation keys produced a very tall row full of repeated Browser client entries, making the row's useful signals hard to scan.
changes.now: The Latest browser column shows the most recently seen web client and the total installation count.

changes.h: iOS context was split across ambiguous columns
changes.was: Clients and device mixed web and iOS hardware, while Build / channel omitted the iOS OS version and required scanning across repeated blocks.
changes.now: iOS hardware lists distinct reported models; iOS software keeps OS version, marketing version, build, freshness status, and release channel together for each iOS client.

changes.h: Desktop density hid the final context column
changes.was: The table's content width pushed Last seen just beyond the normal desktop surface after adding the new support signal columns.
changes.now: Tighter minimums and wrapped user metadata keep all six headers visible at desktop width; the shared table container still scrolls intentionally at narrow widths.

verification: Focused source contracts: App Activity UI and brand-identity tests pass.
Authenticated browser: owner-gated local preview renders the six headers, two iOS clients, and summarized browser activity.
Narrow viewport: the table reports overflow-x: auto with 999px content inside a 563px viewport, preserving access without clipping.
notes: No production deployment was made for this UI slice; the live production page remains unchanged until the implementation is explicitly shipped.
The telemetry identifies a web client, not the browser engine. The label stays Browser client rather than inferring Chrome or Safari.
